ai.description: *Raorchestes manohari* is a small shrub frog (20–25 mm) with a yellowish-brown dorsum and distinct dark brown lateral bands. It is identified by a prominent white spot on the snout and granular skin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes manohari* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or golden-yellow patch on the groin and the hidden surfaces of its thighs.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes manohari* inhabits the high-altitude evergreen forests of the southern Western Ghats, typically found perched on shrubs and trees in misty montane habitats.
ai.behavior: *Raorchestes manohari* is a nocturnal frog that remains active during the night, typically foraging for small insects among the foliage of tropical rainforests.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes manohari* undergoes direct development within terrestrial eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with females laying small clutches in leaf litter.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes manohari* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes manohari* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes emitted from vegetation in evergreen forest habitats.
